says: A control in a presentation (the layout of a policy's input controls) is kept only when its type is one of the eight known ones: text, number box, text box, check box, combo box, drop-down list, list box, multi-line text box. Any other control type is dropped and not shown. A known control is tied to a policy input only when it carries a reference id; one without a reference id is still shown, just not tied to an input.

The localized-text file (ADML) for an ADMX file is chosen in this order, and each step is taken only if the .adml file actually exists in that folder, not merely the folder. First, the folder named exactly like the chosen language code beside the ADMX file. Otherwise, the first sibling folder, in the order the system lists folders, whose language part (before the dash) matches the chosen language, such as de-AT for de-DE, and that holds the file. Otherwise, the en-US folder. The file has the same name as the ADMX with the extension .adml.

A policy input of type list records whether it declares a value prefix: it does whenever the attribute is present, even if empty. The registry value name of any input element, lists included, is the prefix when non-empty; otherwise it is the element's own valueName, when given. A name already set from the prefix is kept.

A localized-text file is refused as invalid when it lists the same text id twice in its string table, or the same presentation id twice in its presentation table. It is also refused when a string or a presentation has no id. Only the first string table and the first presentation table in the file are read. A control in a presentation without a reference id is kept.

An ADMX file is accepted into the loaded set only when both it and its localized-text file load, and its namespace is not already owned; then its categories, products, policies and support rules are held for linking and its namespace becomes owned by it. A file that fails at this stage leaves nothing behind. Faults found later, while linking, are covered by a separate rule.

A category element that has any child nodes but no parent-category child makes the ADMX file invalid; it is reported as 'The ADMX is invalid' and the file is skipped. A category with no child nodes at all is a top-level category.

A policy that has no parent-category reference, or no supported-on reference, is accepted when the ADMX file is read, but the load then stops with an error while linking, instead of skipping that policy or file. The same happens when a child product's parent cannot be found.

When two categories, two products, two support rules or two policies in one ADMX file share a name, the load stops with an error while linking, instead of skipping the file or keeping the first. Items already staged from that file are not removed.

An ADMX file whose target namespace is not listed among its declared namespaces is accepted by the file reader with an empty namespace. The check for an already-owned namespace then stops with an error instead of reporting a load failure for that file.

statement: When linking stops the load with an error, what the person sees depends on the calling screen, which reports a failed load but whose exact message and the state left in the workspace we did not trace.

assumed.why: The linking code raises unhandled errors; their handling lies in the calling screens, outside these blocks.
assumed.ifWrong: A person might see a different message, or be left with a partly loaded set of definitions.

evidence.shows: Linking runs after files are staged, outside the per-file error handling.
